messages:
Morgan: Heads up — product is repackaging plans next month to introduce 'burst credits' and a new per-minute metered rate for free-tier escalations. Early opt-in telemetry shows ~12% increase in sustained GPU hours last week. We need a quick capacity reforecast for 30/60/90d and recommendations for reserved vs on-demand. @Javier can you lead?

Javier: on it. can you share the cohort query you used? i'll run a few uplift scenarios.

Morgan: pasted the rough query I used below — it's a 7-day rolling cohort filter for PLG users + recent opt-ins. quick and dirty:

```
SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day, sum(gpu_seconds)/3600 as gpu_hours
FROM usage_events
WHERE product_line = 'plg' AND event IN ('generation','chat')
  AND plan IN ('free','starter')
  AND ts >= now() - interval '14 days'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 desc
LIMIT 30;
```

Javier: thanks. running baseline -> uplift modeling now. expecting to try +15%, +30%, +60% buckets.

Priya: FYI i already did a quick cohort extrapolation on last week's traffic: baseline = 50k GPU-hrs/mo, conservative uplift ~+18%, median +32%, bursty worst-case +58%. Major delta is in eu-central (higher conversion) and us-west. apac showed low conversion but longer sessions when it happens.

Linh: two things to call out: 1) our rate limits/quotas change will reduce HTTP 429s — that will smooth throughput and likely increase sustained token rate, not just spikes. 2) eu-central has limited rack availability; procuring more GPUs there has a ~8-10 week lead time.

Alex: finance note — if baseline 50k -> median 65k GPU-hrs, that's roughly +30% cost. Reserved commitments buy down unit cost but require a 3mo+ commitment. We need a delta table for reserved vs on-demand across those uplift buckets to decide approval.

Javier: initial shard-level sketch: to support +32% steady-state we need ~45 extra A100-ish equivalent GPUs across clusters (split: us-west +18, eu-central +20, apac +7). For +58% worst-case, ~95 extra GPUs. Those are sustained estimates (24/7).

capacity-bot: Dedicated pool snapshot: 200 GPUs available for short-term burst; automated allocation cap: 14 days per org unless manually extended by infra team.

Priya: if we use short-term dedicated burst for the first 2 weeks post-launch, we should also throttle by route and prefer quantized model variants for cheaper tokens to control spend.

Morgan: good. small routing policy we can flip on day-0: prefer-lite -> prefer-quantized -> fallback-full. That limits token cost while we watch quality.

Linh: routing change will also impact cache hit patterns — make sure redis prefix TTLs are extended during the burst window to avoid cache churn.

Alex: action for finance: i'll draft a quick cost delta sheet. can you put GPU-hrs per region into a simple CSV? Javier?

Javier: will export by EOD. preliminary figures inlined:
- Baseline: 50,000 GPU-hrs/mo
- Conservative (+18%): 59,000 GPU-hrs/mo
- Median (+32%): 66,000 GPU-hrs/mo
- Worst (+58%): 79,000 GPU-hrs/mo

Morgan: ok action items: Javier -> 90-day GPU-hr forecast + per-region breakdown (EOD). Linh -> update rack/procurement lead times and apac mitigation plan (72h). Alex -> finance cost-delta and reserved vs on-demand table (48h). Priya -> routing + model-variant plan + throttles (24h). I'll coordinate with product on launch messaging to estimate customer migration rate. @Javier @Linh @Alex @Priya :thumbsup:

Javier: ack, starting with per-region shard simulation. will post a short summary thread when done.

Priya: noted. i'll also add a small eval set to measure quality delta if we push more quantized variants.

Alex: will loop in finance and legal if we need any short-term contract changes.

Morgan: thanks team. if anyone hits a blocker for procuring short-term capacity ping me directly.

billing-bot: FYI — current committed usage discount tiers will apply only to committed pools; on-demand bursts bill at list unless covered by a new temporary promo.

Linh: small ask — let's set a temporary quota cap policy per-customer to avoid a single account blowing the burst pool. I'll propose limits in the next message.

Morgan: agreed. prioritize per-customer caps + soft-fallback to cheaper models.

Javier: posting initial CSV now in thread. I'll ping when forecasts are in.

Priya: :rocket:
